item.text:
**6B.5 Verdict**
Mixed, leaning yes. Sisi’s 2024 record shows real use of measurement and administrative instruments in education, cash transfers, and public investment management. Transparent correction was partial, not consistent: the strongest reforms were technocratic and often externally supervised, while health and refugee-service changes were rushed, weakly consulted, or regressive.

- **Arab Republic of Egypt: Technical Assistance Report-Public Investment Management Assessment** — IMF — 2024-04-02 — [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/technical-assistance-reports/issues/2024/04/02/arab-republic-of-egypt-technical-assistance-report-public-investment-management-assessment-547051) — The report says Egypt had already taken steps to improve infrastructure access and public investment management through new legislation, information systems, and staff-capacity efforts, and it recommends stronger appraisal, selection, maintenance, procurement, portfolio management, transparent budget reporting, and e-procurement. IDs: 6B.5, 6B.4, 5B.7
- **Egypt: Preparing Students for Life and the Workplace of Tomorrow** — World Bank — 2024-05-21 — [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/05/21/egypt-preparing-students-for-life-and-the-workplace-of-tomorrow) — Education reform used explicit measurement and feedback: new exams, teacher training, quality assurance, digital learning resources, and two rounds of grade-4 assessment; the article also notes concrete implementation problems such as overcrowding, tutoring pressure, and a short school year. IDs: 6B.5, 6B.2
- **Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt through Cash Transfer Programs** — World Bank — 2024-05-28 — [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs) — Takaful and Karama is described as having a targeted delivery system based on proxy means testing, a grievance mechanism, and a dynamic social registry; the ministry also produced case studies, videos, and a depository, which are strong signs of monitored and iterated social-policy delivery. IDs: 6B.5, 6B.4, 6B.2, 6B.3
- **Under the patronage of President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, the Administrative Control Authority holds a launching ceremony for the third phase of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy 2023-2030** — Administrative Control Authority — 2024 — [URL](https://aca.gov.eg/News/3173.aspx) — The launch framed the new phase around transparency, integrity, anti-corruption frameworks, and improving public services, but this is framework-level signaling rather than proof of service outcomes. IDs: 6B.5, 5B.7
- **Egypt: New law threatens to reduce access to healthcare for millions** — Amnesty International — 2024-07-30 — [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-new-law-threatens-to-reduce-access-to-healthcare-for-millions/) — Sisi ratified Law 87 of 2024 without adequate consultation; the law lets private actors run public health facilities for profit without price regulation, which is the opposite of transparent corrective stewardship. IDs: 6B.5, 6B.2, 6B.4
- **Egypt: Education Restricted for Refugees** — Human Rights Watch — 2024-12-02 — [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/egypt-education-restricted-for-refugees) — Refugee children were kept out of school by residency requirements, fees, and discrimination; that shows weak correction and poor feedback from service failure, especially for a vulnerable population. IDs: 6B.5, 6B.2, 6B.3
- **Egypt: President al-Sisi must reject new asylum law which violates refugee rights** — Amnesty International — 2024-12-03 — [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/12/egypt-president-al-sisi-must-reject-new-asylum-law-which-violates-refugee-rights/) — The asylum law was rushed, lacked meaningful consultation, broadened discretionary power, and failed to protect education, housing, and social-security rights; that is strong negative evidence on transparent correction. IDs: 6B.5, 6B.2, 6B.3
- **Egypt: Halt Crackdown on People Voicing Concerns Over Economic Crisis** — Amnesty International — 2024-05-13 — [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/) — When people criticized prices, living conditions, and service failures, authorities responded with arrests and abuse rather than open correction, which weakens the case for evidence-based service improvement. IDs: 6B.5, 5B.7

**Search gap**
- I found strong process evidence for measurement in education, cash transfers, and public investment management.
- I did not find equally strong independent evidence of a government-wide service-delivery dashboard, routine publication of outcome indicators, or open complaint loops in health, housing, or social services.
- The most convincing positives are technocratic and program-specific; the most convincing negatives show that when service failures became politically sensitive, correction was often delayed, rushed, or repressive rather than transparent.
